items.followUp: Define the OSI model and explain the function of the data-link layer.

rubric.why: Defines a network model as a framework for communication.
rubric.description: A computer network model is a layered framework that explains how devices communicate and how data is transmitted over a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a definition that describes a framework or model for network communication.

rubric.why: States a correct function of an OSI layer.
rubric.description: The application layer provides network services to applications used by the user.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct explanation of the application layer.

rubric.why: States a correct function of an OSI layer.
rubric.description: The transport layer manages end-to-end delivery of data and may divide it into segments for transmission.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct explanation of the transport layer.

rubric.why: States a correct function of an OSI layer.
rubric.description: The network layer selects routes and forwards packets toward their destination using logical addresses.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct explanation of the network layer.

modelAnswer: A computer network model is a layered framework that explains how devices communicate and how data is transmitted over a network.
The application layer provides network services to applications used by the user.
The transport layer manages end-to-end delivery of data and may divide it into segments for transmission.
The network layer selects routes and forwards packets toward their destination using logical addresses.

items.followUp: What is phishing? Explain how it can be used to commit cybercrime.

rubric.why: Defines cybercrime as unlawful activity involving computers or networks.
rubric.description: Cybercrime is an illegal activity carried out using a computer, digital device, or network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: Identifies and explains a type of cybercrime.
rubric.description: Hacking is gaining unauthorised access to a computer or network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming hacking and explaining unauthorised access.

rubric.why: Identifies and explains another type of cybercrime.
rubric.description: Phishing uses deceptive messages or websites to obtain a person’s private information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming phishing and explaining how it is used to obtain information.

rubric.why: Gives a further type of cybercrime and an explanation.
rubric.description: Gives another valid type, such as identity theft, cyberstalking, malware attacks, online fraud, software piracy, or cyberbullying, with a suitable explanation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one further valid type with an explanation.

modelAnswer: Cybercrime is an illegal activity carried out using a computer, digital device, or network.
Hacking is gaining unauthorised access to a computer or network.
Phishing uses deceptive messages or websites to obtain a person’s private information.
Identity theft misuses another person’s personal details.

Other types include cyberstalking and cyberbullying, which harass people online; malware attacks, which can damage a computer; online fraud, which can deceive people into losing money; and software piracy, which involves copying software in violation of copyright.

items.followUp: State two ways a flowchart can help when checking an algorithm.

rubric.why: Recognises that a flowchart presents solution steps visually.
rubric.description: A flowchart shows the steps of a solution visually.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing its visual or graphical representation of solution steps.

rubric.why: States a practical benefit of a flowchart in problem solving.
rubric.description: A flowchart makes the problem-solving logic easier to understand, helps communicate the solution, or makes errors or missing steps easier to find.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid benefit.

modelAnswer: A flowchart shows the steps of a solution visually, making the problem-solving logic easier to understand.
It helps communicate the solution and can make errors or missing steps easier to find.

items.followUp: What three things should be identified when analysing a problem?

rubric.why: Describes problem analysis as careful study and understanding of a problem.
rubric.description: Problem analysis is the careful study and understanding of a problem before designing its solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the study or understanding of the problem.

rubric.why: States the purpose of analysis: identifying what is required to solve the problem.
rubric.description: Problem analysis identifies the required inputs, processing, and expected outputs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the problem’s requirements, such as its inputs, processing, and outputs.

modelAnswer: Problem analysis is the careful study and understanding of a problem before designing its solution.
It identifies the problem’s required inputs, processing, and expected outputs.
